# FDG7009

> CONSIDER using exception builder methods.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 7.1 Exception Throwing.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1510, CA1511, CA1512, CA1513
- Automatic fix: yes
- Severity: library suggestion, application suggestion, test suggestion
- Status: verified

CA1510 to CA1513 report an argument null, null-or-empty, range or disposed check that throws a new exception instead of calling the framework's throw helper, which is the builder method of this rule for those checks; they report only when the target framework has the helper (.NET 6 to .NET 8). Builder methods for a library's own exceptions are not seen, so coverage is partial. Each has an SDK code fix that calls the helper and changes no signature. Builder methods that return the exception must not be public (FDG7008).

## From the book

It is common practice to throw the same exception from different places. To avoid code bloat, use helper methods that create exceptions and initialize their properties.

Also, members that throw exceptions are less likely to be inlined. Moving the throw statement inside the builder might allow the member to be inlined. For example:

```csharp
class File{
  string fileName;

  public byte[] Read(int bytes){
    if (!ReadFile(handle, bytes)) ThrowNewFileIOException(...);
  }

  void ThrowNewFileIOException(...){
    string description = // build localized string
    throw new FileIOException(description);
  }
}
```
